scientific_question: Does repeated adaptive floor use alter final topology or sensitivities?
minimum_matrix: At least benign and hard full optimization trajectories with original floor, fixed floors, and guarded adaptive policy
notes: Completed six fixed-floor 40-iteration controls plus two true guarded adaptive 40-iteration in-loop trajectories. The guarded cantilever run selected 1e-12 for 16 iterations and 1e-3 for 24; the guarded bridge run selected 1e-12 for 19 and 1e-3 for 21. Both completed 40/40, max accepted true residual <1e-6, no guard-failure fallbacks, and no 1e-2 selections. This is a narrow two-case addendum, not a broad trajectory-invariance suite.

scientific_question: How much do raised floors perturb compliance sensitivities?
minimum_matrix: Sensitivity-difference metrics for fixed-floor controls and selected-floor cases
notes: Completed for all 24 held-out true-keep cases using the floor-substituted Bernoulli convention: all 72 solves converged; fixed 1e-3 and 1e-2 floors give mean solid-sensitivity relative L2 shifts 0.340 and 0.555, with max shifts 0.988 and 0.998.

scientific_question: Does floor escalation solve a materially different equilibrium problem?

notes: Only 3/12 reference-floor direct solves meet 1e-6 residual; sparse hard references remain ill-conditioned, so robust moderate-size reference work is still open.

scientific_question: Which GMG component controls the admissibility boundary?
minimum_matrix: Locked sweeps over smoother, level count, precision path, restart length, tolerance, and iteration budget on representative hard cases
notes: Completed 42 representative cases across canonical, 3-level, Jacobi smoother, W-cycle, no root correction, tol=1e-5, and tol=1e-7 variants. All variants passed 6/6 except no_root_correction, which passed 3/6, indicating root-local correction is the material stack component in this matrix.

scientific_question: Is the p_SIMP=4.5 admissibility boundary stable under standard exponents?
minimum_matrix: Repeat representative direct/GMG policy cases for p=3, p=4, and p=4.5
notes: Completed both fallback-only and tuned-threshold policy sweeps. Tuned policy: 36/36 pass, 27 predicted raises, 9 predicted keeps, zero false keeps; p=3.0, 4.0, and 4.5 each retain the same accepted-floor counts of 1e-12:3, 1e-3:7, 1e-2:2.

scientific_question: Would less extreme original floors avoid most failures?

notes: Completed both fallback-only and tuned-threshold policy sweeps. Tuned policy: 48/48 pass with zero false keeps; rho0=1e-12, 1e-9, and 1e-8 each accept floors 1e-12/1e-9/1e-8:3, 1e-3:7, 1e-2:2; rho0=1e-6 accepts 1e-6:4 and 1e-3:8.
